6.q: Give the correct order of steps in the sociological explanation of a delivery rider's accident that goes beyond blaming the rider.
6.a: The explanation runs: (1) Note the platform's algorithm sets a ten minute delivery guarantee (2) Treat the guarantee as a piece-rate structure where each minute of delay costs the worker (3) Link the incentive to chronic road risk taking rather than personal recklessness (4) Conclude that the accident expresses the platform's management of time, a structural cause open to study and change. A wrong answer that stops at rider carelessness shows the student has missed that sociological explanation uncovers structural connections behind individual acts.

5.q: Trace the correct sequence of links by which the oppressive factory simultaneously bred workers' collective strength.
5.a: The dialectic runs: (1) The factory concentrates workers under one roof and one clock (2) Mechanical routine and regimented labour destroy craft autonomy and degrade skill (3) Shared exploitation gives workers common grievances to discuss (4) Concentration enables communication, collective functioning and concerted efforts for better conditions. A wrong answer that sees only oppression or only liberation shows the student has missed the dialectical claim Marx made about factory life.

6.q: Give the correct order of stages in a participant observation study of gig workers at a metro waiting area.
6.a: The study runs: (1) Enter the setting daily during peak hours as an ordinary customer (2) Reveal the researcher's identity gradually to a few workers after trust forms (3) Adopt a participant-as-observer role helping with small tasks and learning their slang (4) Weigh the limits of the setting, where visibility and turnover constrain long immersion. A wrong answer that begins with interviews alone shows the student has missed that participant observation trades surveys for sustained immersion in daily life.

5.q: Give the correct order of points in the Durkheimian critique of calling a whole culture inherently suicidal.
5.a: The critique runs: (1) Separate the social fact of a national rate from any individual case (2) Apply integration and regulation theory to ask which groups inside the country carry the rate (3) Refuse the ecological fallacy of reading a statistical aggregate as a cultural essence (4) Demand comparative analysis of structural variables before naming any culture at all. A wrong answer that treats the rate as proof of national character shows the student has missed Durkheim's rule that social facts must be explained by other social facts.

6.q: Give the correct order of stations a domicile certificate application passes through in an ideal-typical collectorate.
6.a: The procedure runs: (1) The clerk with fixed jurisdiction accepts only the specified documents (2) The file moves up the graded hierarchy from superintendent to the collector's office (3) Every action is recorded in written documents preserved as the file (4) Trained staff applying conduct rules hand over the certificate, keeping the office separate from the person. A wrong answer that lets personal contacts replace any station shows the student has missed that each Weberian feature is designed to make authority calculable rather than arbitrary.
